column1: # The mode line the CLI draws under its input box.
# The launcher sends nothing to a session until the pane shows the input box
# with one of these lines somewhere under it:
#     ❯                              the input, opened by the prompt glyph
#     ────────────────────────       a rule, the last one on the pane
#       a status line of the user's  any number of lines
#       ⏵⏵ accept edits on …         the mode line: a row of this table
# The box is recognised by its shape. This table is the second half of the
# evidence: a line under the box has to be a mode line. Text that only
# appears somewhere on the pane is not evidence: a dialog can quote a mode
# line and a shell can echo one.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   id       short name
#   pattern  how the line begins, mode symbol included
#   basis    seen      drawn by the real CLI in a pane, and read from it
#            inferred  built by the same rule as the rows that were seen, or
#                      taken from another release, and not seen
#   where    under     a mode line, under the box
#            inside    how the CLI marks a folded paste, inside the box
# A line matches a row when it starts with the pattern. A narrow pane cuts
# the line short ("⏵⏵ accept edits" at 20 columns, "⏵⏵" at 12), and a cut
# line matches when what is left is the start of the pattern and holds at
# least the symbol. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# The rows marked seen were drawn by CLI 2.1.330, started in a pseudo-terminal
# with no credentials and a temporary home directory, at 100 columns; the
# accept-edits row also at 40, 25, 20, 16 and 12, replayed through tmux 3.3a.
# The bypass row is inferred. Starting the CLI with permissions bypassed to
# look at it is refused in this repository, on purpose. In that release the
# mode's title is "Bypass Permissions", its symbol is the one accept-edits
# uses, and every seen row is the symbol, the title in lower case, and "on".
# If a session launched with --bypass is at its prompt and the launcher says
# the prompt never appeared, this is the row to correct.
# The shortcuts row is inferred too. 2.1.330 was seen to draw that hint only
# after the mode ("⏸ manual mode on · ? for shortcuts"), at 100 and 40
# columns, never at the start of the line; releases that drew no mode for the
# default one began the line with it.
# A user's own status line is drawn between the box and the mode line. It was
# seen with one, three and six lines, and with a line opening with the prompt
# glyph; the mode line was the last line each time. Its length and wording do
# not matter here.
# The row marked inside is not a mode line. Once the launcher has pasted,
# the CLI folds a paste of five lines or more, or one very long line, into
# "[Pasted text #1 +10 lines]" (or "[Pasted text #1]"), and for about eight
# seconds draws "paste again to expand" where the mode line was. The look
# before an Enter therefore also accepts a box that shows the paste: this
# marker, or the start of the text itself when the CLI shows a short paste
# as it is. Seen in 2.1.330 at 80, 40 and 20 columns, with and without a
# status line of the user's own. It plays no part before a paste.
